messages.subject: Functional pattern with Shiny
parts:
I have question about how to model an app with R/Shiny.

I have an existing R script that consists of 4 functions that do various things using input parameters and provide different pieces of output.

In the interests of reducing function complexity I have functions do 1 thing.  This means the entire processing involves all 4 functions being called with data from 1 passed to the next.

The functions work well from an R script but now I want to build a shiny app to allow a user to input the initial values and then push a button to fire off the processing.

I need to limit (isolate) each Input field and only start the processing when each field is complete.

The challenge is that I want to display output data from each function to the UI.

I can do it for the first function :

 output$tab1 <- renderDataTable({
     
   if (input$process == 1){
   
     isolate({
       dat<-function1.data(city=paste(input$city, " ", input$country)
       as.data.frame(dat$df)  
       })
             
     }},options=list(paging= FALSE)
       )

But how I can build the others.  I think the issue I have is that I need to display different functions output in different render functions.

The only way forward it seems is to call all 4 function for each UI element.  This is not good as the functions involve a bit of processing.  Any ideas?

messages.subject: Re: Functional pattern with Shiny
parts:
I think I figured it out.   I changed the Action button to a Submit button as this prevents an interactivity.   I then wrapped the function calls into reactive() objects.

Not fully tested but it seems to be doing what I need.

Lee

messages.subject: Re: Functional pattern with Shiny
parts:
It's hard to say whether you're on the right track or not without more specifics. It sounds like you have this to start with:

a <- function(x) {...}
b <- function(x) {...}
c <- function(x) {...}
d <- function(x) {...}

And you're essentially calling d(c(b(a(...)))), is that right?

The reactive version of this, if you didn't want to modify the original functions, would be like this:

rA <- reactive(a(input$foo))
rB <- reactive(b(rA()))
rC <- reactive(c(rB()))
rD <- reactive(d(rC()))

Then your outputs could access any of rA, rB, rC, or rD by invoking them like a function.

Does that help?
